evidence.basis: Controlled amplitude and wavelength definition demand.

hints: Name the greatest displacement and the reference position from which it is measured.
walkthrough: Identify the changing quantity as displacement of a particle or point on the wave.
Amplitude is the greatest value of this displacement measured from equilibrium.
State the controlled definition: the maximum displacement of a particle or point on a wave from its equilibrium position.

ai_rubric.observable: Defines amplitude as the maximum displacement of a particle or point on a wave from equilibrium.

hints: Refer to adjacent points at the same stage and specify the shortest separation.
walkthrough: Points in phase are at the same stage of their cycle.
Choose adjacent in-phase points so the separation is the shortest spatial repeat.
State the controlled definition: the minimum distance between two adjacent points on a wave that are in phase.

ai_rubric.observable: Defines wavelength as the minimum distance between adjacent in-phase points, or gives an accepted equivalent.

evidence.basis: Direct retrieval from the verified Lesson 1 handoff.

hints: Track the disturbance and one marked section of rope separately.
walkthrough: The bead moves only after the pulse reaches it, so energy has reached a new place.
A marked rope section moves locally and does not ride with the pulse.
Therefore energy travels with the disturbance while the rope sections move locally, so option B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, identifying energy transfer with local motion of rope sections.

evidence.basis: Amplitude distinguished from signed displacement and peak-to-peak distance.

hints: Measure from equilibrium to one extreme, not between both extremes.
walkthrough: The extremes are equally far from equilibrium: 4.0 mm in either direction.
Amplitude is the maximum displacement size, so it is positive and equals 4.0 mm.
The 8.0 mm separation between extremes is peak-to-peak distance, so option C is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C, giving an amplitude of 4.0 mm.

evidence.basis: Phase reasoning from stage of oscillation rather than displacement alone.

hints: Compare both the displacement and the direction of motion.
walkthrough: Equal displacement places both points at the same height relative to equilibrium.
One point is on the upward part of its cycle while the other is on the downward part, so their stages differ.
They are not in phase; option B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, recognising that opposite motion directions mean different stages of the cycle.

evidence.basis: Period extraction followed by reciprocal frequency calculation.

hints: Period is the total time divided by the number of complete cycles.
walkthrough: Known values: 12 complete oscillations take 4.8 s.
Calculate the time for one oscillation: T = 4.8 s / 12.
This gives T = 0.40 s.

ai_rubric.observable: Divides the total time by 12 complete oscillations.
Obtains a period of 0.40 s with a valid time unit.

hints: Use the reciprocal relationship between period and frequency.
walkthrough: Carry forward T = 0.40 s from part (a).
Use f = 1/T.
Substitute: f = 1 / 0.40 s = 2.5 s⁻¹ = 2.5 Hz.
Check: 2.5 cycles per second for 4.8 s gives 12 cycles.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses f = 1/T or divides the number of cycles by the total time.
Obtains a frequency of 2.5 Hz with a valid frequency unit.

evidence.basis: Read amplitude and spatial repeat, then convert a wavelength fraction to phase.

hints: Measure vertically from equilibrium to an extreme.
walkthrough: The equilibrium line is at zero displacement.
A crest is at +3.0 cm, so the maximum displacement from equilibrium is 3.0 cm.
The amplitude is 3.0 cm.

ai_rubric.observable: Reads the maximum displacement from equilibrium as 3.0 cm.

hints: Use the horizontal separation of adjacent points at the same stage.
walkthrough: Adjacent crests occur at x = 2.0 cm and x = 10.0 cm.
Their separation is 10.0 cm - 2.0 cm = 8.0 cm.
The wavelength is 8.0 cm.

ai_rubric.observable: Reads the separation of adjacent crests as 8.0 cm.

hints: Express the P-to-Q separation as a fraction of the wavelength, then use 360° for a full cycle.
walkthrough: P is at x = 2.0 cm and Q is at x = 4.0 cm, so Δx = 2.0 cm.
From part (b), λ = 8.0 cm.
The separation is Δx/λ = 2.0/8.0 = 1/4 of a cycle.
Phase difference = (1/4) × 360° = 90°.
The result is consistent with moving from a crest to the next equilibrium crossing.

ai_rubric.observable: Determines the P-to-Q separation as 2.0 cm.
Expresses the separation as 2.0/8.0 = one quarter of a wavelength.
Obtains a phase difference of 90° with a valid angular unit.

evidence.basis: Original mixed application combining current wave quantities with the Lesson 1 energy-transfer model.

hints: Find cycles per second first, then take the reciprocal.
walkthrough: Known values: 15 oscillations take 6.0 s.
Frequency is cycles per unit time: f = 15/6.0 = 2.5 Hz.

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains the frequency as 2.5 Hz with a valid frequency unit.
Obtains the period as 0.40 s with a valid time unit.

hints: Compare the cork separation with the crest separation, then multiply that cycle fraction by 360°.
walkthrough: The spatial separation is Δx = 0.30 m and the wavelength is λ = 0.80 m.
The cycle fraction is Δx/λ = 0.30/0.80 = 0.375.
Phase difference = 0.375 × 360° = 135°.
This lies between a quarter cycle, 90°, and a half cycle, 180°, as expected.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the spatial fraction 0.30/0.80 of one wavelength.
Obtains a phase difference of 135° with a valid angular unit.

hints: Track the travelling disturbance separately from one region of water.
walkthrough: The ripple is a progressive disturbance that advances from R toward S.
Neighbouring regions interact, so the disturbance and its energy are passed onward.
Each water particle oscillates locally about equilibrium and has no net journey from R to S.
Thus energy reaches S without the water at R travelling there.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the progressive disturbance transfers energy through neighbouring regions to S.
States that water particles near R oscillate locally and do not travel to S.
